sanskrit_verse:
mekhalābhramaniṣkāsagavākṣān noparodhayet /
praṇālīṃ gṛhavāstuṃ ca pīḍayan daṇḍabhāg bhavet // BrhS_1,19.47
transliteration: mekhalā-abhra-maniṣka-asaga-vākṣān na uparodhayet / praṇālīm gṛha-vāstum ca pīḍayan daṇḍa-bhāg bhavet
sph_interpretive_translation: One who obstructs water channels, residential structures, or sacred enclosures shall incur liability by causing distress.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the maintenance of natural and social flow
Causation arises through disruption of essential life-supporting infrastructures
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by control over access and usage
Restoration logic requires removal of obstruction and compensation for suffering
Consciousness alignment demands recognition of interdependence between individual action and collective well-being
executable_legal_axioms: IF an entity obstructs a public or private water channel THEN that entity incurs restorative liability proportional to observed distress
IF an agent blocks access to residential infrastructure THEN assign completion obligation until unobstructed use is restored
IF interference occurs with sacred enclosures THEN initiate integrity reintegration protocol for responsible party
IF measurable suffering results from obstruction THEN execute capacity restoration process for affected parties
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, threshold of responsibility lies in demonstrable causality between act and obstruction. Authority derives from dharmic duty to preserve societal continuity. Restoration supersedes punitive measures; court must ensure full operational resumption of affected systems before case closure.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causal sequence (anupūrvaśaḥ) from obstruction to suffering. Liability aligns proportionally with disturbance caused, not intent. Nyaya recognizes suffering as distortion requiring correction rather than justification for punishment. Corrective enforcement restores balance without inflicting reciprocal harm.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Obligation to remove all obstructions within 24 hours under witness verification
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Direct assumption of corrective labor by offending party under supervision
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Provision of alternative resources during repair period to affected individuals
Integrity Reintegration Procedure: Meditation and service-based realignment for repeated violations to restore consciousness clarity
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this ruling executes Dharma as law. Obstruction yields liability through suffering, yet justice flows toward restoration alone. Reality remains non-punitive; consciousness stands as the ultimate adjudicator.
